title: Rational inequalities and sign charts
terms: rational inequality; sign chart; critical endpoint; strict inequality; interval notation.

exposition.text:
To solve P(x)/Q(x) > 0, first exclude every zero of Q. Factor numerator and denominator
and mark all real zeros on the number line; the sign is constant on each intervening interval. A
factor of odd multiplicity changes sign when crossed, while one of even multiplicity does not.
Test one point in each interval or track signs systematically. For a nonstrict inequality, include
numerator zeros that are in the domain; never include denominator zeros. Cancelling a common
factor simplifies signs but does not restore an excluded point. Multiplying an inequality by an
expression of unknown sign requires splitting into cases or retaining its sign information.

solution.text:
Away from x = 1, the squared factor is positive, so the sign is that of (x + 2)/(x − 3), which
is negative on (−2, 3). Include the zero at −2 and the internal zero at 1, but exclude the
pole 3. This gives [−2, 3).

question.text:
What is the sum of the integer solutions of 1/(x − 1) > 1/(x + 2) with −5 ≤ x ≤ 5?
(A) −5 (B) −3 (C) 0 (D) 2 (E) 5

solution.text:
Subtracting gives 3/[(x − 1)(x + 2)] > 0, so x < −2 or x > 1. The allowed integers are
−5, −4, −3, 2, 3, 4, 5, whose sum is 2.

The original domain excludes 1 and 3. After cancellation the sign is that of (x − 1)(x +
2)/(x − 3), which is nonnegative on [−2, 1) and (3, ∞). The cancelled point 1 remains ex-
cluded even though it appears as a zero in the reduced numerator.

For which real a does > 0 hold for every real x ̸= 2?
2
(x − 2)
(A) −2 < a < 2 (B) −2 ≤ a ≤ 2 (C) a < 2 (D) a > −2 (E) a = 2 only

solution.text:
The denominator is positive on the domain, so the numerator must be positive there. If
|a| < 2, its discriminant is negative and its leading coefficient positive. At a = ±2 it van-
ishes at x = ∓1, a permitted input. If |a| > 2, it is negative on an interval, which cannot
be removed by excluding the single point 2.

The numerator changes sign at ±2, the denominator at ±1. Their signs agree outside
[−2, 2] and inside (−1, 1); zeros at ±2 are included and poles at ±1 are excluded.
